blocks.text: Tool execution prompts cover actually calling a selected tool correctly, extracting the right parameters from the current context, formatting them in the exact shape the tool expects, validating the call before it runs, and parsing the result back into the agent ongoing context.

This topic covers extracting and formatting correct parameters, validating a tool call before execution, handling execution errors explicitly, parsing results back into context, and retrying a failed call, the mechanical follow-through after tool selection, covered in an earlier topic, has already chosen which tool to use.
1. Tool Selection vs Tool Execution, Revisited

blocks.alt: Tool Selection vs Tool Execution, Revisited
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473806793-94570592.png

Tool selection, covered in an earlier topic, decides which tool to use, tool execution is the distinct follow-up concern, actually calling that selected tool with the correct parameters in the correct format, so it genuinely does what was intended.

2. Extracting the Correct Parameters
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473806794-617902684.png

Given a user request and a selected tool, the model needs to extract the specific parameter values that tool actually requires, a search tool needs a specific query string, a calculator needs specific numbers and an operation, this extraction step connects directly to the structured outputs concepts covered in an earlier module.
3. Formatting Parameters in the Exact Expected Shape

blocks.alt: Formatting Parameters in the Exact Expected Shape
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473807743-65680436.png

Extracting roughly the right information is not enough, the parameters need to match the tool exact expected format, a date parameter expecting a specific format like year-month-day will fail if given a relative phrase like tomorrow without being converted first, this connects directly to schema-based outputs, covered in an earlier module.

blocks.text: 4. Validating a Tool Call Before Executing It

blocks.alt: Validating a Tool Call Before Executing It
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473807744-760456717.png

This connects directly to output validation, covered in an earlier module, before actually executing a tool call, especially one with real consequences, sending an email, making a purchase, validating that all required parameters are present and correctly typed catches a malformed call before it causes a real, potentially hard to undo effect.

blocks.title: This validation step matters more as tool consequences grow more serious
blocks.content: A tool call that only retrieves information carries little risk if malformed, a tool call that takes an irreversible real world action deserves a genuinely more careful validation step before execution.

blocks.text: 5. Handling a Tool Execution Error Explicitly

blocks.alt: Handling a Tool Execution Error Explicitly
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473807745-634998017.png

When a tool call actually fails during execution, a network error, an invalid parameter the tool itself rejects, this needs to be handled explicitly, fed back to the agent as an observation it can reflect on, connecting directly to reflection prompts covered earlier in this module, rather than silently treated as if the call had succeeded.
6. Parsing the Tool Result Back Into Context

blocks.alt: Parsing the Tool Result Back Into Context
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473807745-849269715.png

Once a tool call succeeds, its result needs to be parsed into a form the agent can actually use in its next reasoning step, this connects directly to the structured outputs concepts covered in an earlier module, a cleanly parsed result is far easier for the agent to reason about correctly than raw, unstructured tool output.
7. Retrying a Failed Tool Call

This connects to the output validation retry pattern covered in an earlier module, a failed tool call, whether from a malformed parameter or a transient error, can often be retried, ideally with the specific failure reason fed back to help correct the next attempt, rather than simply abandoning the entire step after one failure.
8. A Worked Tool Execution Example

An agent selects a calendar booking tool for the step "schedule a meeting for next Tuesday," extracts the relative date reference, converts it to the tool required exact date format, validates that a required time parameter is also present before executing, and correctly parses the confirmation result back into its ongoing trajectory context.
9. Tool Execution Prompts and the Function Calling Module

This topic covers the conceptual, prompting-level side of tool execution, the actual API-level mechanics of function calling, how a specific provider structures tool definitions and call requests, is covered in full technical depth in the later Function Calling and Tool Calling module.
Worked Example

A team building a task automation agent finds their calendar booking tool occasionally fails silently, the agent extracts a relative date like next Tuesday but passes it directly to a tool expecting an exact calendar date, and the resulting error goes unnoticed until a user reports a missing appointment.

Adding explicit parameter format conversion before execution, plus validation confirming the tool call succeeded and explicit error handling feeding any failure back to the agent as an observation, catches this exact class of failure immediately going forward, with the agent now able to retry or ask a clarifying question rather than silently failing.
Common Mistakes

items: Extracting roughly correct parameter values without converting them to the exact format the tool actually expects
Executing a tool call without validating it first, especially for a tool with real, potentially irreversible consequences
Treating a failed tool execution as if it had succeeded, rather than explicitly handling and feeding back the failure
Not parsing a tool raw result into a usable form before the agent tries to reason about it in the next step

blocks.text: Practice

Take a tool with a specific parameter format requirement, write a prompt that extracts parameters from a natural language request and converts them into that exact required format, and consider what validation check should happen before this tool call actually executes.
Key Takeaway

Tool execution prompts handle the mechanical follow-through after tool selection, extracting and correctly formatting parameters, validating a call before it runs, handling execution errors explicitly rather than silently, and parsing results back into usable context, with validation deserving extra care for any tool carrying real, consequential effects.
